meta.incidence_unit: affected births per 100,000 live births (global, approximate unless basis=cited)
meta.note: Seed catalogue curated from established gene–disease relationships (OMIM/Orphanet) and representative incidence figures. Incidence varies by ancestry and consanguinity; values are global order-of-magnitude anchors pending the Orphanet prevalence + GBD 2023 pulls, which the ingest layer will fold in per DATA_NEEDED.md.

diseases.name: Congenital heart disease (multifactorial)

CS.note: multifactorial; no single-gene carrier screening for the common forms

PGT.note: not a single-gene disorder in most cases

NBS.note: pulse-oximetry screening for critical CHD + surgery mitigates

diseases.editing_note: Not selection/editing-addressable as a monogenic trait; detection + surgical repair mitigate.

diseases.name: G6PD deficiency
diseases.incidence_source: very common in malaria-endemic regions; hundreds of millions affected globally

CS.note: carrier/at-risk testing; population screening in endemic areas

PGT.note: usually mild; embryo selection rarely pursued

NBS.note: NBS in some regions; avoid oxidant triggers, manage neonatal jaundice

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable; usually mild so rarely pursued.

diseases.name: Familial hypercholesterolaemia

CS.note: dominant; cascade screening of relatives used, not preconception carrier screening

PGT.note: PGT-M possible but rarely pursued given treatability

NBS.note: highly treatable with statins; child screening/cascade used, not classic NBS

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable; treatability makes reproductive intervention uncommon.

diseases.name: Sickle cell disease

NBS.note: NBS + penicillin prophylaxis/hydroxyurea; gene therapy emerging

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable; affected×affected couples fall to the S1 residual.

diseases.name: Down syndrome (trisomy 21)

CS.note: aneuploidy; screened via maternal-age/cfDNA, not carrier screening

NBS.note: not preventable postnatally; associated conditions managed

diseases.editing_note: PGT-A/selection-addressable; whole-chromosome aneuploidy not an editing target.

diseases.name: Orofacial clefts (cleft lip/palate)

CS.note: multifactorial; no routine carrier screening for nonsyndromic clefts

PGT.note: not a single-gene disorder in most cases

NBS.note: surgical repair postnatally, not an NBS target

diseases.editing_note: Not selection/editing-addressable as a monogenic trait; surgically correctable.

diseases.name: Alpha-thalassaemia

NBS.note: Hb Bart's lethal in utero; HbH managed but no early-life cure

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable (both-carrier couples have unaffected embryos).

diseases.name: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

CS.note: dominant; identified via family history, not carrier screening

NBS.note: adult-onset; no early-life mitigation

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when a parent carries a known variant.

diseases.name: Neural tube defects

CS.note: multifactorial; folate supplementation is the primary prevention, not carrier screening

PGT.note: not a single-gene disorder; embryo selection not applicable

PND.note: maternal serum AFP + ultrasound detect open defects

NBS.note: structural at birth; prevented antenatally by folate, not NBS

diseases.editing_note: Not selection- or editing-addressable as a monogenic trait; folate fortification is the key lever.

diseases.name: Clubfoot (talipes equinovarus)

PGT.note: not a single-gene disorder in most cases

NBS.note: newborn exam + early Ponseti casting corrects most cases

diseases.editing_note: Not selection/editing-addressable as a monogenic trait; early casting mitigates.

diseases.name: Beta-thalassaemia

NBS.note: no early-life cure prevents transfusion dependence broadly

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY)
diseases.incidence_source: ~1/650 male births; per 100k total births (affects males)

NBS.note: testosterone therapy later, not NBS

diseases.editing_note: PGT-A/selection-addressable; aneuploidy not an editing target.

diseases.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1

CS.note: dominant; ~50% de novo, carrier screening not meaningful

NBS.note: clinical surveillance; not an NBS target

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when a parent carries a known variant.

diseases.name: Cystic fibrosis

NBS.note: NBS + CFTR modulators / early care

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable (both-carrier couples have unaffected embryos).

diseases.name: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (DiGeorge)

CS.note: usually de novo microdeletion; carrier screening not meaningful

PGT.note: PGT-A/PGT-SR or targeted testing when a parent carries the deletion

NBS.note: not an NBS target; associated conditions managed clinically

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable; contiguous-gene deletion not an editing target.

diseases.name: Congenital sensorineural deafness (GJB2/DFNB1)
diseases.incidence_source: GJB2 a leading cause of ~1/1000 congenital deafness

NBS.note: newborn hearing screen + cochlear implant/early intervention transforms outcome

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Fragile X syndrome
diseases.incidence_source: full mutation ~1/4,000 males, ~1/8,000 females; per 100k total births

NBS.note: no disease-modifying early therapy

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Marfan syndrome

CS.note: dominant; ~25% de novo, so carrier screening not meaningful

NBS.note: managed clinically (beta-blockers/surgery); not an NBS target

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when a parent carries a known variant.

diseases.name: Edwards syndrome (trisomy 18)

CS.note: aneuploidy; screened via cfDNA, not carrier screening

NBS.note: usually lethal in infancy; no mitigation

diseases.editing_note: PGT-A/selection-addressable; aneuploidy not an editing target.

diseases.name: Turner syndrome (45,X)
diseases.incidence_source: ~1/2,500 female births; per 100k total births (affects females)

NBS.note: growth hormone/estrogen management later, not NBS

diseases.editing_note: PGT-A/selection-addressable; monosomy not an editing target.

diseases.name: Tuberous sclerosis complex

CS.note: dominant; ~2/3 de novo, carrier screening not meaningful

NBS.note: clinical surveillance; not an NBS target

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when a parent carries a known variant.

diseases.name: Myotonic dystrophy type 1

CS.note: dominant; identified via family history, not carrier screening

PGT.note: PGT-M for known parental repeat expansion

NBS.note: no early-life mitigation; congenital form supportive care

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when a parent carries the expansion.

diseases.name: Spinal muscular atrophy

NBS.note: presymptomatic gene therapy / nusinersen transforms outcome (NBS)

diseases.editing_note: Selection- and NBS-addressable; a leading NBS success story.

diseases.name: Duchenne muscular dystrophy
diseases.incidence_source: ~1/5,000 male births; per 100k TOTAL births (affects males)

CS.note: DMD carrier testing in female relatives/panels

PGT.note: PGT-M / sexing for known maternal variant

NBS.note: some NBS pilots; early steroids/exon-skipping partially mitigate

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when maternal variant known.

diseases.name: Haemophilia A
diseases.incidence_source: ~1/5,000 male births; per 100k TOTAL births (affects males)

NBS.note: manageable with factor VIII/emicizumab; not standard NBS

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when maternal variant known.

diseases.name: Phenylketonuria (PKU)

NBS.note: classic NBS success: dietary Phe restriction prevents disability

diseases.editing_note: NBS + diet essentially prevents the disease phenotype.

diseases.name: Patau syndrome (trisomy 13)

CS.note: aneuploidy; screened via cfDNA, not carrier screening

NBS.note: usually lethal in infancy; no mitigation

diseases.editing_note: PGT-A/selection-addressable; aneuploidy not an editing target.

diseases.name: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (MCAD)

NBS.note: classic NBS success: avoid fasting prevents metabolic crises/death

diseases.editing_note: NBS + fasting-avoidance largely prevents the phenotype; selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase)

NBS.note: NBS + glucocorticoid replacement prevents fatal salt-wasting crisis

diseases.editing_note: NBS mitigates; selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Huntington disease

CS.note: dominant; identified via family history/predictive testing, not carrier screening

PGT.note: PGT-M, incl. exclusion testing to avoid disclosing parental status

NBS.note: adult-onset; no early-life mitigation

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable for a heterozygous parent; only a viable homozygous-affected parent (all embryos affected) would lack an unaffected embryo — couple-config dependent, handled in S1.

diseases.name: Retinoblastoma (heritable)

CS.note: dominant; family-based testing, not carrier screening

PGT.note: PGT-M for known parental RB1 variant

NBS.note: no NBS, but surveillance exams in at-risk infants improve survival

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when a parent carries a known variant.

diseases.name: Achondroplasia

CS.note: dominant; ~80% de novo, carrier screening not meaningful

PGT.note: PGT-M when an affected parent carries the recurrent variant

NBS.note: no early-life mitigation of the skeletal phenotype

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable for affected parents; most cases de novo.

diseases.name: Wilson disease

NBS.note: highly treatable early (chelation/zinc) prevents organ damage

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy

NBS.note: presymptomatic HSCT/gene therapy; added to NBS panels (US RUSP)

diseases.editing_note: Selection- and NBS-addressable.

diseases.name: Gaucher disease

NBS.note: type 1 responds to enzyme replacement; early Rx mitigates

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Friedreich ataxia

NBS.note: no early-life therapy that meaningfully alters course

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Classic galactosemia

NBS.note: NBS + galactose-free diet prevents neonatal sepsis/death

diseases.editing_note: NBS + diet mitigates; selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Haemophilia B
diseases.incidence_source: ~1/30,000 male births; per 100k TOTAL births (affects males)

NBS.note: manageable with factor IX; gene therapy emerging; not standard NBS

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when maternal variant known.

diseases.name: Fabry disease

NBS.note: ERT/chaperone therapy; on some NBS panels

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Metachromatic leukodystrophy

NBS.note: presymptomatic gene therapy (atidarsagene) transforms early-onset outcome

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Mucopolysaccharidosis I (Hurler)

NBS.note: presymptomatic HSCT/ERT improves outcome; on some NBS panels

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Maple syrup urine disease

NBS.note: NBS + branched-chain-restricted diet prevents encephalopathy

diseases.editing_note: NBS + diet mitigates; selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Hunter syndrome (MPS II)

NBS.note: ERT available; earlier treatment improves outcome

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable when maternal variant known.

diseases.name: Tay-Sachs disease
diseases.incidence_source: elevated in founder populations; global rare

NBS.note: no effective therapy; uniformly fatal in infancy

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable; affected individuals do not reproduce (S1 ~0).

diseases.name: Canavan disease
diseases.incidence_source: rare globally; elevated in Ashkenazi founders

NBS.note: no effective therapy; progressive and fatal

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

diseases.name: Niemann-Pick disease type A
diseases.incidence_source: rare globally; elevated in Ashkenazi founders

NBS.note: no effective therapy for type A; fatal in early childhood

diseases.editing_note: Selection-addressable.

rollup.note: Bottom-up point sums over the curated catalogue. Coverage is partial (a seed catalogue of the highest-burden serious conditions), so totals are a LOWER BOUND on the full genetic-disease denominator and will rise as the Orphanet/GBD ingest expands the library. The parametric Monte-Carlo model provides the calibrated top-down denominator with credible intervals.
